reviews.title: Honestly just seems like you’re paying a lot of money for some widgets.
reviews.text:
I used to have this app on Android, and I paid for the full lifetime version. It worked great. When I moved over to iPhone, I was bummed they didn’t have this app. When I heard they did after 2 years, I jumped on it. However, after inquiring about whether I could transfer my lifetime membership from Android to Apple, I got no response, which speaks to their customer service being non-responsive at best and complacent at worst. As for the actual functionality of the app, YOU have to do all the things yourself. YOU basically turn your iPhone into a “Great Value” version of the Minimalist Phone app, and the app gives you a step-by-step guide on how to change all your phone settings to make it mimic the originally intended version of the app (hopefully you remember all the settings you changed!). I assume this is because Apple doesn’t play nice with this app. Alas. Anyways, what Minimalist Phone actually provides (that you might not have had before) are simple widgets that allow you to put your apps in list form (and not the default picture form). That’s it. You’re paying $20 a year on up for a list-widget. Everything else you can do yourself via changing settings on your phone, or using the ReFocus app.

For all these reasons, I am not happy and regret paying an additional $20 for my first year despite having a lifetime subscription.

reviews.title: What am I paying for?
reviews.text:
I paid for a year because I liked the idea of less phone in my life and reducing the addictive features of my phone. The app basically walks you through setting up existing iPhone settings to eliminate color from your phone and helps you set up time limits on specific apps. Great, but not sure why I’m paying a third party for that. 

I personally don’t like the widgets that turn your apps into a list. It has made it very difficult for me to find anything on my phone. I could spend a significant amount of time rearranging apps to make them more accessible but then it’s more time on my phone. Also, some apps redirect through the widget/shortcut before opening which is annoying. An example is Safari. 

I thought this would be a game changer but after using it for over a month, I will probably get rid of the widgets and go back to color. Honestly, the black and white Home Screen doesn’t make that big of a difference if the apps themselves are full color. 

It’s a good idea in theory but, for me, not that great in practice.
